change.title: pr-8
change.description: FIX: proper handling of group memberships
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 pages for 50 members at limit 50, and 3 for 100. On the real last page `showingLast` is false, so Next sets `offset = min(0+50, 50) = 50` (line 33) and loads an empty page that shows as "2/2" with no members. The same thing happens when an admin removes the only member on the last page (51 → 50 members, offset 50). Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`, keeping the 0 case for empty groups.

findings.title: Adding a user who is already a member raises a 500, and it can leave a partial add behind
findings.body: `group.add(user)` is `self.users.push(user)` (app/models/group.rb:272-274). On a persisted group that inserts the GroupUser row right away. `group_users` has a UNIQUE index on (group_id, user_id) (app/models/group_user.rb:18), and GroupUser has no uniqueness validation, so pushing an existing member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. The old `usernames=` path diffed against the current members, so this never happened. The admin UI hits this easily: the selector is never cleared after Add (the `// TODO: should clear the input` at admin-group.js.es6:62), so pressing Add a second time resends the same names. Any names before the duplicate stay added, and the client shows no error. Skip users who are already members (for example `next if group.users.include?(user)`, or diff against `group.users.pluck(:username)`), and add a spec for it.

findings.title: Response shape changed, but spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb still expects an array
findings.body: `members` now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`. spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb:76-84 still runs `JSON.parse(response.body).map{ |m| m['username'] }`. On a Hash each `m` is a `[key, value]` array, so `m['username']` raises TypeError and those examples fail. Update the spec to read `['members']` and assert on `meta`.

findings.title: Public group members page now silently shows only the first 50 members
findings.body: Before, `/groups/:name/members` returned every member of a non-automatic group (200 for automatic ones). The endpoint now defaults to `limit 50` (groups_controller.rb:22), and the group-members route calls `model.findMembers()` with the model's default `limit: 50, offset: 0` (group.js:10-11). This template has no pager and no total count, so a group with more than 50 members shows a truncated list with no hint that anyone is missing. Add the same previous/next controls the admin page has, or show `user_count` and a way to load more.

findings.title: addMembers/removeMember failures are silent
findings.body: Neither `addMembers` nor `removeMember`, nor the controller actions that call them (admin-group.js.es6:56, 64), handle a rejection. Discourse.ajax rejects on a 422 or 500 (mixins/ajax.js:51-68), and nothing catches it, so a failed add or remove leaves the list unchanged with no message. Show the server's error, for example with `bootbox.alert`, the way other admin actions do. Clearing `usernames` after a successful add would also take care of the TODO.

findings.title: Does `group.users.delete(user_id)` keep the `user_count` counter cache in sync?
findings.body: The existing `Group#remove` (app/models/group.rb:276-278) destroys each GroupUser, which runs the `counter_cache: "user_count"` callback on GroupUser (group_user.rb:2). On a has_many :through, `users.delete` removes the join rows with delete_all by default. Depending on the Rails version, that may skip that counter, so the admin groups list (BasicGroupSerializer's `user_count`) could show a stale count after a reload. Have you checked this? Using `group.remove(User.find(user_id))` would match the existing helper.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT while the route is DELETE
findings.body: The route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (config/routes.rb:49), but this example sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`. Controller tests dispatch straight to the action, so the test passes without exercising the real verb. Use `xhr :delete` to match the route and the example at line 125.

findings.title: limit/offset are not bounded
findings.body: `limit` and `offset` come straight from params. A negative value makes Postgres raise (LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative), which returns a 500, and any caller who can see the group can pass a huge limit. Consider clamping them, for example `limit = [[limit, 1].max, 200].min` and `offset = [offset, 0].max`.

contracts.equivalent_path: Discourse.Group#findMembers called from the route's setupController
contracts.before_after: Sets offset on the group model, then refetches the page; findMembers clamps the offset to user_count and copies meta back onto the model

contracts.equivalent_path: Old update_put path with group.usernames=, which diffed additions against current members
contracts.before_after: PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members, then findMembers reloads the list; the input is never cleared
contracts.visible_effect: The members list refreshes on success

contracts.visible_effect: The list reloads; user_count on the client comes from meta.total (a live count)
contracts.failure_mode: The rejection is not handled, so the failure is silent; the DB counter cache may go stale (unverified)
contracts.open_question: Does has_many :through delete with an id decrement the GroupUser counter_cache in this Rails version?

contracts.action: Public group members page loads members
contracts.before_after: Sets the group as the model and calls findMembers without awaiting it; the template iterates `members`
contracts.visible_effect: Only the first 50 members render, with no pager
contracts.failure_mode: A rejection is silent and the list stays empty

summary: The pull request swaps the old "replace all usernames" group editing for paginated member lists and separate add/remove endpoints. Three things are wrong today. The admin pager's totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit, which lands the admin on an empty last page. Adding a user who is already a member raises a unique-index 500, and the selector's never-cleared input makes that easy to hit. The public group members page now silently cuts the list at 50 members with no pager. The members response also changed shape, but the existing spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb was not updated, so those examples will fail. Smaller points: add/remove failures are silent in the client, the remove_member spec uses PUT instead of DELETE, limit/offset are not bounded, and I have a question about whether user_count stays in sync after removal.
